findings.title: Non-float invalid inputs raise decimal.InvalidOperation, not TypeError
findings.evidence: The guard only rejects float; any other non-Decimal value is stringified and handed to Decimal, so parse_money(None) or parse_money(True) or parse_money([1]) raises decimal.InvalidOperation (an ArithmeticError), bypassing the TypeError contract implied by the float check.
findings.evidence_quote: amount = value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
findings.recommendation: Whitelist accepted types explicitly: accept str, int (excluding bool) and Decimal, raise TypeError otherwise; keep the str conversion only inside that branch so callers can reliably catch TypeError.

findings.title: quantity type is never validated before the negative check and multiply
findings.evidence: The only quantity check is a bare numeric comparison, so line_total with a str or None quantity dies with an unhelpful TypeError from the comparison, and a float quantity slips past the check and only fails later at Decimal times float inside the return expression; bool is silently accepted as 1.
findings.recommendation: Validate quantity up front: isinstance(quantity, int) and not isinstance(quantity, bool), or Decimal; raise TypeError for anything else, then check negativity. This also makes the float rejection consistent with parse_money.

findings.title: No tests cover the rounding and validation behaviour
findings.evidence: The change is entirely money rounding logic (half-up quantize on unit price times quantity and on tax) and no test command was run; the float-rejection branch, the negative-quantity branch, the half-up boundary (e.g. 1.005 to 1.01) and the InvalidOperation cases above are all unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for: float price rejected, negative quantity rejected, half-up rounding at the cent boundary, Decimal vs str vs int price equivalence, and the invalid-type cases identified above.

findings.title: Rounding depends on the ambient thread-local decimal context
findings.evidence: quantize and the multiplications run against the caller's thread-local decimal context; if any code in the process lowers getcontext().prec (or enables Inexact/Rounded traps), parse_money either raises InvalidOperation for values with more digits than the configured precision or produces different results, with no protection inside this module.
findings.recommendation: Perform the arithmetic inside decimal.localcontext() with an explicit precision (and explicit traps) so money results do not depend on process-global decimal state.
